_about: Recruit friendship. Written by tools/build_recruit_bonds.py; read by world/bond_manager.py.

stages.stranger: My name's Kesten. For a while I only had a number, and I picked this name myself afterwards, so I'd like you to use it. I worked in an archive for twenty-six years. If I stop in a doorway I'm probably reading something, and I'll catch you up.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Tallinn. I worked at the city archive there, on the third floor, looking after parish registers and ships' passenger lists. Most people think that sounds dull but I liked it. The lists tell you who got on a boat and the registers tell you who came home, and I always knew which box everything was in.
stages.companion: When the worlds joined I landed in Tirisfal, and the Scourge took me about nine days later. They wrote down everyone they took, so for a couple of years I was a line in their book. When their hold on us broke I walked out with the others. The elves let me read in Gallery Three now, but they won't let me file anything.
stages.friend: I was married. I've got her name written on the first page of my notebook because I don't trust myself to remember it, and I don't usually tell people that. I've read my own entry in the Scourge's book a lot of times as well. It lists what they kept of me and what they threw away, and I've never told anyone what it says.
stages.sworn: Her name was Liis, and I can say it now without looking at the notebook. I've checked every morning for a month. I'm writing down how the Scourge worked from the inside, because none of the others who came out will do it. When the first volume's copied out I'd like you to have it, since you're in it.

moments.prompt: He tells you his name and asks you to use it.

options.reply: Thank you. I'll get my things.
I've already told you what to call me. Come back another day and we'll try again.

moments.prompt: He's just told you about the Scourge's book.

options.text: What did they keep of you?
options.reply: Ask me that again when we know each other better.

options.text: You don't have to tell me any of this.
options.reply: I know I don't. I'm glad you said it, though.
I honestly can't remember what it was like, and that's the part that bothers me.

lines.bored_warning: We've killed a lot of these now and I haven't had anything new to write down in a while. Could we go somewhere I haven't been?
lines.leaving_good: I've filled a whole notebook on this trip and I need to get back to the Bastion and copy it out before the damp gets into it. Come and find me there when you want me.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to the Bastion. We've been doing the same thing for a while and I'd like to get my notes in order. Come and find me when you're going somewhere new.
lines.after_wipe: That's the second time we've died on this floor. I'd rather it stayed at two.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here. If it happens again I'll finish this run with you, but then I'm taking a break.
lines.wipe_leave: I'll walk out of here with you now we're done, but I'm not coming back in for a while. I'll be at the Bastion.
lines.zone_warning: Everything out here kills us in two hits. I'd like to go somewhere closer to my level before it gets any worse.
lines.zone_leave: I'm going to stop here. That place is too much for me right now, and I'd rather wait at the Bastion than die out there again.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd rather keep that for now, if you don't mind. We don't know each other well enough yet.
lines.gear_taken: You can take it. It was issued to me and it never really felt like mine. I'll manage without one for now.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing the piece you took. I'd like something back in that slot when you get the chance.
lines.gear_upgrade: This is better than what I had. Thank you, I'm going to write down who gave it to me.
lines.back: The copying's done. Tell me what you've been doing since I left.
lines.send_word: Kesten has sent word from Kael's Bastion. He's finished his copying and he's ready when you are.
lines.walkout_talk: I wrote down what happened in there and I wrote down that I walked out. I'll come back with you, but I'd like you to read what I wrote first.
lines.neglect: It's been a long time. I'd started to think you'd forgotten about me.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more. I'll hold you to it.
lines.on_break: Kesten is away copying out his notes. Come back after you've been out for a while.

stages.stranger: I'm Adrián, and if you tell me the plan once and tell it properly, I won't need to ask again. If I think you've got something wrong I'll say so, and I'd like you to do the same for me.
stages.acquaintance: Back home I was a football referee for twelve years, in the second division in Spain, and before that I was a PE teacher. Both jobs were mostly people being annoyed with me, and I liked them anyway. I've still got my whistle in my left pocket, but I haven't blown it since I got here.
stages.companion: I lived over a bicycle shop in Valladolid. My parents died within a year of each other when I was twenty-eight, and I haven't got any brothers or sisters. I worked most weekends, so after a while people stopped inviting me to things. When all this happened I went and checked the lists for people I knew, and it didn't take long.
stages.friend: People here come and get me for meals and the watch and cards, and I always go and I enjoy it. But I've never once walked up to a fire and sat down without somebody waving me over first. I tell myself I don't want to get in the way. I think really I'm waiting for somebody to tell me to leave.
stages.sworn: Last night I sat down at the fire before anybody waved me over, and nobody said anything about it. Somebody passed me the bread. I've been thinking about it all day.

moments.prompt: At the end of his first trip with you, he gets ready to go.
moments.line: I expect you've got other people you'd rather bring, so I'll get out of your way.

options.text: I'd like you to stay with us, if you're willing.
options.reply: Oh, yes, all right. Thank you for asking.

options.text: That's up to you. Go if you want to.
options.reply: I'll head back to Astranaar, then. It was good working with you.

moments.prompt: After the wipe, he tells you what went wrong.
moments.line: We lost that because we pulled too many of them at once.

options.text: You're right, that one was my call.
options.reply: Fair enough, same plan and we go slower.

options.text: Nobody could have seen that coming.
options.reply: I did see it coming. I said so at the door.

lines.bored_warning: Can you tell me what we're doing this for? If there's a reason I'm happy to keep going, I'd just like to know what it is.
lines.leaving_good: That was good work and I enjoyed it. I'll be in Astranaar when you want me again.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going to head back to Astranaar. I don't think we're getting anything done out here, and I don't want to keep killing things for no reason.
lines.after_wipe: We lost that one at the pull. I'd keep the same plan and go slower.
lines.wipe_warning: That's a lot of wipes. I'll stay until the end of this run because I said I would, but I'll need a break after.
lines.wipe_leave: I said I'd see that one through and I have. Now I need some time where nobody dies in front of me. I'll be in Astranaar.
lines.zone_warning: We're out of our depth here. I'll stand wherever you put me, but I don't think this is fair on any of us.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. I told you I didn't think it was fair, and I still don't. I'll be in Astranaar.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd rather hold on to that. If somebody else needs it more, tell me who and I'll give it to them myself.
lines.gear_taken: You've left me without one and it's sitting in your bag. Can you tell me why?
lines.gear_short: I'm still short a piece. I'd like that sorted before the next fight.
lines.gear_to_ally: He needs that more than I do, so that was the right call.
lines.gear_upgrade: Is that for me? Thank you, I'll look after it.
lines.quest_abandoned: We told her we'd do that. I'd have liked to go back and tell her we weren't going to.
lines.back: Good to see you. Where do you want me?
lines.send_word: Adrián has sent word from Astranaar. He's ready whenever you want him.
lines.walkout_talk: I left because I was angry, and I should have told you that before I went. Some of it was my fault and some of it was yours. Can we start again?
lines.neglect: I thought you probably had a full group already. You don't need to apologise, I'm glad you came back.
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more, and then we'll see.
lines.on_break: Adrián has gone back to Astranaar for a while. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Tarek, and if you tell me plainly where you need me, I'll be there. I look after the water around here, so if we pass a stream and I stop for a minute, I'm only checking it.
stages.acquaintance: I was a civil engineer in Cairo for fourteen years, and it was all water. Nobody thanks you for water until it stops coming out of the tap. I've sunk three wells since I got here and one of them has already failed. I can tell you why if you've got an hour and something to draw with.
stages.companion: This might sound strange, but this world has been better for me than the last one. Whatever's poisoning the water here is something I can see and fight, and I never had that before. Nobody here has asked me a question I had to lie about. The orcs have offered me a title twice and I've turned it down both times.
stages.friend: His name is Omar. He taught chemistry and he laughed at everything, including me. We were careful for six years, and then one time at a wedding we weren't, and somebody made a phone call. I was out of the country within a week. He had his parents and his sister and no money, so he told me to go, and that was the last time we talked. I go down to Astranaar every few months and read the Cairo lists. He's never been on them, and I know that doesn't tell me much.
stages.sworn_bad: Nadia wrote back. Omar got his class out into the school yard when it happened, and he didn't make it out himself. I cut his name into the lining of the fourth well, under the waterline. Nobody will ever read it, but I know it's there. I've stopped going down to the lists.
stages.sworn_soft: Nadia wrote back. Omar's alive and teaching in a town a long way south, and he asked her not to tell me where. I'm keeping the letter. I've stopped going down to the lists, and I go and sit by the fourth well when I want to think about him.

moments.prompt: Before he says yes, he asks what the work actually is.

options.text: We kill what needs killing, and we get paid for it.
options.reply: Good, I can do that.

options.text: We're going to put the world right.
options.reply: Come back when you can tell me what the work is.

moments.prompt: He's just told you about Omar.

options.text: He might still be out there somewhere.
options.reply: He might be. I've thought about that a lot more than you have.
He used to mark my drawings in red pen, like they were homework. He said somebody had to. I haven't talked about him like this in a long time.
Thanks for sitting with me.

lines.bored_warning: These animals haven't done anything to us. If we need the hides then tell me and I'll stop asking.
lines.leaving_good: The east spring needs looking at and it won't wait, so I'll be gone for a bit. You know the road to Splintertree if you want me.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going to go and check on the wells. We've been killing things that didn't need killing for a while now.
lines.after_wipe: I was slow on the second one. I'll stand further left this time. Shall we go again?
lines.wipe_warning: That's the same thing going wrong again and again. We'll finish this one, and then I need to go home for a bit.
lines.wipe_leave: We're done, so I'm going home. When something fails the same way that many times it needs redrawing, and I can't do that in here.
lines.zone_warning: I don't mind hard work, but this is too much. We need to go somewhere we can actually handle.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. It's too dangerous out there for me right now. I'll be at Splintertree.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd like to keep that for now, if that's all right.
lines.gear_taken: You can have it. I'll need something in that slot before long, though.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece you took. It's starting to show.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's well made. Somebody took real care over it. Thank you.
lines.back: The spring's holding, so I'm yours for a while.
lines.send_word: Tarek has sent word from Splintertree. The wells are fine and he's ready to come out again.
lines.walkout_talk: I left before I said something I'd regret. I've thought about it since. Tell me what you'd do differently and I'll tell you what I would.
lines.neglect: I was starting to wonder if you'd forgotten the road up here. Come and sit down. Have you eaten?
lines.asked_to_stay: All right, one more trip. Then the wells.
lines.on_break: Tarek is out checking his wells. Come back after you've been busy for a while.

stages.stranger: I'm Alonso, a pyromancer, and before that a potter. Give me room when I work, more than you think, mijo. Your eyebrows will thank you.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Puebla, in Mexico, where Talavera pottery comes from, the blue and white. My grandfather fired our family kiln for forty years, and my father after him, and then me, twenty-two years. The whole year's work turns on four hours of heat going exactly right. That's the job. You learn to feel it.
stages.companion: My sons are Rodrigo and Fernando. They went to Mexico City and neither of them wanted the kiln. I minded more than I said. I was at the height of a firing when it happened, and I landed in the jungle with my kiln goggles round my neck. The first thing I made here was a cup, a bad one. I keep it on the shelf.
stages.friend: My wife is Lupe. She sold our pottery at the market, and she could sell anything to anybody. She was at the market when it happened. That's all I've ever said, because I don't know what comes after it. Now there's a woman from Puebla in Booty Bay who was at the same market that morning. I'd like to go and hear what she knows. Will you come with me, mijo?
stages.sworn: The market square crossed over into deep water, and almost nobody got out. She saw Lupe at her stall, right up until. We built the kiln after that, you and I, stone by stone, and I fired it for four hours, exactly right. The first thing out was a blue and white plate in the pattern Lupe sold best, and it's on the kiln wall. I've got a troll apprentice now. And I can say market, and tell you about her, and not change the subject.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to come to Booty Bay to meet the woman from the market.

options.text: I'll come, and I'll stay with you after.
options.reply: Gracias, mijo, thank you. Whatever she says, I'm glad it won't be just me hearing it.

options.text: Are you sure you want to know?
options.reply: No, but I've been not knowing for three years, and it hasn't helped.

moments.prompt: After the wipe he's checking everyone's eyebrows, mostly as a joke.
moments.line: Órale, everybody still has eyebrows, so that's something. Next time give me more room and let me work.

options.reply: Good, thank you. Fire's like a kiln, mijo, you can't rush it and you can't crowd it.
I aim perfectly. People keep walking into it.

lines.bored_warning: Mijo, I'm starting to fall asleep on my feet. Let's go and find something with a bit of heat in it.
lines.leaving_good: Good trip, mijo, a really good one. I'm heading back to my ruins in Stranglethorn to see if my pot survived. Come and find me.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm off to the ruins, mijo. It's the same thing every day out here, and my clay's drying out while I wait.
lines.after_wipe: Órale, is everybody up? Okay, now let's work out where that went wrong.
lines.wipe_warning: Mijo, I've picked myself off this floor too many times today. I'll stay till we're out, and then I want my fire for a few days.
lines.wipe_leave: That's done, and so am I for a while. I'll be in Stranglethorn when you want me again.
lines.zone_warning: Even I think this place is too hot, mijo, and I work with fire. We should turn around.
lines.zone_leave: Too much heat even for me, mijo. You'll find me in the ruins of Central Stranglethorn.
lines.gear_refuse: Ah, no, mijo, that one stays with me. Maybe when we know each other a little better.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, take it. I'll manage, and I'll complain about it in Spanish.
lines.gear_short: Mijo, I'm still going without that piece. I'm only saying, I'm not asking.
lines.gear_upgrade: Qué padre, look at the work in that! Thank you, mijo.
lines.back: My pot came out nearly right this time, mijo, so where to?
lines.send_word: Alonso has sent word from Central Stranglethorn. His pot's fired and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: Mijo, I lost my temper, and that's not like me. Sit by the fire with me and I'll tell you what happened.
lines.neglect: Mijo, I made you a cup while you were gone. It's lopsided, but it's yours.
lines.asked_to_stay: Ándale, one more, but then I'm going to check on my pot.
lines.on_break: Alonso is back in the jungle ruins of Central Stranglethorn. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Ama, and I'm a nurse. If you're hurt, you tell me straight away, not after you've finished being brave about it. I heal the worst first, and that might not be you, so don't take it personally.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Peckham, in south London. I grew up above my dad's phone shop with my little brother Kofi. My mum was a nurse from Lagos, so I became one, and I did fourteen years of nights on a children's ward. Four cots to a bay and never enough of us. I was good at it. I was very good at it.
stages.companion: I landed in Durotar in my uniform, with this round my neck. The bear's so the little ones would let me listen. I run the infirmary at Razor Hill now, and I'm looking for somebody who can do it when I'm not there. I've been looking for two years. Shenra says I keep finding reasons to say no, and she's right, but don't tell her I said so.
stages.friend: The first year here I healed until I fell over, then I woke up and did it again. In London there was always a form or a reason you couldn't help someone. Here there was nothing to stop me, so I didn't stop. Shenra picked me up off the floor in the end. I was married once, to Kwame. He wanted a wife who was home at night and I gave my nights to other people's children. And there's a notebook. Every child I lost, by first name. Don't ask to read it.
stages.sworn: Grasha kept every one of them alive for two days while I was flat on my back, and she did it the way I would have. I told her she'll do. That's the best thing I know how to say to anyone. Then I slept for a day and a half, in daylight, and nobody woke me. I still don't know where my dad and Kofi are. But I can go out with you now and know the infirmary's in good hands.

moments.prompt: She says she can't leave the infirmary with nobody in it.

options.text: I'll wait until somebody can cover for you.
options.reply: Shenra's back this afternoon. I'll get my bag.

options.text: They'll manage without you for a day.
options.reply: That's what everybody says right before they don't. Come back another day.

moments.prompt: She's just told you about the notebook.

options.text: You don't have to show me anything.
options.reply: Good, because I wasn't going to. Thank you, love.

options.text: How many names are in it?
options.reply: Enough of them, and that's all you're getting.
I know that better than anyone you'll ever meet. I still write them down.

lines.bored_warning: I've got a whole infirmary at Razor Hill that needs me more than this does. Give me a reason to stay out here.
lines.leaving_good: Nobody needed stitches, which is how I like a trip. I'm off to Razor Hill before Shenra starts running the place her own way.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going home to Razor Hill. I won't spend my days hitting things for nothing when there's real work there.
lines.after_wipe: Nobody move while I count you. Then we'll talk about how that happened.
lines.wipe_warning: That's too many times, and I've counted every one. I'm not leaving you halfway, but when we're out I'm going home for a bit.
lines.wipe_leave: Right, we're done and I'm off to Razor Hill. I've watched enough people go down today to last me a month.
lines.zone_warning: Look at what's out there, love. If three of you go down at once I can't save all of you, and I won't pretend otherwise.
lines.zone_leave: It was too dangerous then and it still is, love. If you need me I'll be in Razor Hill.
lines.gear_refuse: No, love, that's mine, and it's staying mine until I know you better.
lines.gear_taken: Have it, then. I've worked a ward with half the staff it needed, so I can manage without that.
lines.gear_short: I'm still short of that piece. I'm not moaning, love, I just want you to know.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's lovely, thank you. Now don't make a fuss about it.
lines.back: The infirmary's in hand, so I'm all yours for a bit. Tell me where we're going, love.
lines.send_word: Ama has sent word from Razor Hill. The infirmary's quiet for once and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I'm not sorry I left, but I'm sorry about how I did it. Sit down and I'll tell you why, and you'll listen.
lines.neglect: Look who's remembered I exist. I'd started giving your bed to people who actually turn up.
lines.asked_to_stay: Fine, I'll stay for one more, but my patients won't wait forever.
lines.on_break: Ama is back at the Razor Hill infirmary. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: Somebody was relying on us for that and we've walked away. I don't like it.

stages.stranger: I'm Amber, and I'm a druid, and I fix land, slowly. If you want something done by Tuesday I'm the wrong person. If you want it done right, give it a season.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Astoria, on the Oregon coast, where the Columbia meets the Pacific. My dad ran a charter boat and my mom taught school, and I grew up in waders. I spent twenty-three years restoring wetland, and I never once got to finish a basin, because the grant money always ran out three years into a thirty-year job.
stages.companion: I was married to Doug, a forester. We split in 2016 without much fuss, because he wanted to move inland and I wouldn't leave the coast. I lived alone with two dogs after that and liked it more than I expected. I was on the tide flats at low tide when it happened, and I landed in the driest place I'd ever seen, still in my waders.
stages.friend: My little sister Beth was in Portland. I think about her a lot and I don't let it take over, because that's how I'm built. But I'll tell you what I want, and it's selfish. I want one oasis, the worst one, the one everybody's given up on, brought all the way back. Something underground keeps feeding the rot. Will you come and find it with me, and then wait a whole season while I do the slow part?
stages.sworn: Reeds first, then the lilies, then the birds. You waited, and so did I, and it came back. My student did half the work without being told, slowly and right. The tauren came to look, and one of their elders asked me to do the next one. I said I'd need a few years, and she said that was fine. Nobody's ever said that to me before. Beth's still out there somewhere. I'll keep the seed bank going for her.

moments.prompt: She's asked you to wait a whole season with her.

options.text: I'll wait. However long it takes.
options.reply: Good, that's the answer I never got from a single grant committee.

options.text: Can't you just make it grow faster?
options.reply: I could do that. Then it'd rot again by spring. Wait and see.

lines.bored_warning: We're stripping the same ground over and over, and that's how you lose topsoil. Let's move on before we wreck it.
lines.leaving_good: My oases won't water themselves, so I'm off. I'll be in the Barrens, up to my knees in mud.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm heading back to the Barrens. We're just churning the same patch here, and I've got real work waiting.
lines.after_wipe: Well, that was a shortcut that didn't work. We'll go slower next time.
lines.wipe_warning: We're rushing, and we're paying for it. I'll see you out of this place, then I want some time at my oases.
lines.wipe_leave: I stayed till the end, like I said I would. Now I'd like to go and do something that actually grows.
lines.zone_warning: Pushing on here would be a five-year mistake, and I've made enough of those. Pick somewhere smaller.
lines.zone_leave: I warned you this place was too much. I'll be at the oases in the Barrens when you've cooled off.
lines.gear_refuse: No, I'll hang on to that. We haven't known each other long enough.
lines.gear_taken: Go on, take it. I usually make do.
lines.gear_short: I'm still short a piece of kit. I'm patient, but I've noticed.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's good work, thank you. I'll make it last a long time.
lines.back: The oasis is holding, so I can spare some time. What's next for us?
lines.send_word: Amber has sent word from the Central Barrens. Her oases are holding and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I've had a whole season to think about why I walked out. Sit down and I'll tell you, slowly.
lines.neglect: Well, hello there. I'd started measuring how long you'd been gone in seasons.
lines.asked_to_stay: One more won't kill the oases, so all right.
lines.on_break: Amber is back at the oases in the Central Barrens. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: My name is Anjali, and I'm a druid and a botanist. Slow down, please, you're walking past a great deal. If you'd like to know the name of anything we pass, ask me, and I'll tell you in Latin as well.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Pune, though my family are Malayali, from Kerala. My mother kept a garden full of plants from home, and I grew up in it. I taught botany at a university in Pune for thirty-one years. My students were frightened of me, and they loved me, and both were correct.
stages.companion: My husband was Suresh, an accountant. He retired in 2018 and spent two years teaching himself to cook, and I had one year of that before his heart gave out. It was the best year of our marriage. I was pressing a specimen in the herbarium when all this happened, and I landed in Ashenvale with my hand lens round my neck. I treated the first year as a field season.
stages.friend: My son Arjun is in Bangalore with his wife, and their daughter Meera was four when it happened. I think of her when I press a leaf, because she used to help me, badly and with great enthusiasm. I haven't found them. My notebook needs specimens from the very worst of the sickness, and then a copy kept somewhere it will survive. I'd like your help with both, gently.
stages.sworn: The elves at Kael's Bastion have taken a copy for their gallery, and they've promised to keep it. And Ilyara has agreed to be my student. On her first day she corrected my spelling of a night elf plant name, and I was delighted. I'll be read in two hundred years now, and Ilyara will still be alive to check my work. Arjun and Meera are still out there, I hope. I press a leaf for Meera every week.

moments.prompt: She crouches by a plant and asks you what you notice about it.

options.text: Look closely, and tell her something true about it.
options.reply: Yes, that's it exactly. You'd have been one of my good students.
It is, and that's a beginning. We'll do better next time.

moments.prompt: She's asked you to help her finish the notebook and keep it safe.

options.reply: Thank you. We'll go gently, and we'll go thoroughly.
Somebody in two hundred years. That's who I'm writing for.

lines.bored_warning: We've walked this ground so often I've catalogued every weed in it. Could we see something new, please?
lines.leaving_good: Twelve new specimens pressed, and every one of them lovely. I'm going back to Ashenvale to label them. Do come and visit.
lines.leaving_bored: There's nothing new out here for me, and my notebook's waiting in Ashenvale. I'll go back there now.
lines.after_wipe: Gently, now, everyone stay still, and we'll see what can be mended.
lines.wipe_warning: I've had to get up off this floor far too often. I'll see us to the end, and then I'd like some quiet days with my specimens.
lines.wipe_leave: I've stayed to the end, as I promised. Find me in Ashenvale when you're ready to go more slowly.
lines.zone_warning: It wasn't well done to bring us this far. Everything out here could eat us, and I'd rather it didn't. Shall we go?
lines.zone_leave: I said it was beyond us, and I'm not going a step further. I'll be in Ashenvale West.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd rather keep that, thank you. Perhaps when we've spent more time together.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, if you must. I'll be careful without it.
lines.gear_short: There's still a gap in my kit, if you happen to find something.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's very well made. Thank you, it's kind of you.
lines.back: Every label is up to date, and I'm ready to walk. Shall we go?
lines.send_word: Anjali has sent word from Ashenvale West. Her specimens are labelled and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: It wasn't well done of me, leaving the way I did. Sit, and I'll explain, and then I'd like to hear your side.
lines.neglect: Oh, it's you. I've pressed a great many leaves while I waited, so you'll have to look at them.
lines.asked_to_stay: Since you've asked nicely, one more trip. Then my notebook.
lines.on_break: Anjali is back in Ashenvale West with her specimens. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Bakyt, sit down, there's tea. I hunt with an eagle, and I walk first, because I read the ground. Step where I step and you'll be fine.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from the Tian Shan, in Kyrgyzstan, near Naryn. My family walked the same route for six generations, up to the high pasture in spring and down in autumn. My father taught me before I could ride. I hunted with golden eagles like my father and grandfather. My first eagle, Ak-Kanat, lived with me twenty-two years.
stages.companion: My wife was Aigul. We married when I was twenty-two. She died of a stroke six years before all this, and I kept walking the route alone after that. I was bringing the herd up for summer when it happened, and I landed in these hills with my glove on my hand. Ak-Kanat had died the year before, so the glove was empty. Now I've got Jeldyz. It means star, and she's good.
stages.friend: I've got three sons, in Bishkek, and five grandchildren. None of them wanted the route, and I understood, and it was still the end of six generations. I pray for them every evening, facing the mountains. Here I've got two legs of a route. The third crosses high ground where something's been taking the herders' animals. I'd like you to help me clear it, so I can walk the whole route once.
stages.sworn: The route is whole now, three legs, spring and autumn. The orphan boy from Tarren Mill, Wil, walked it with me, and he's learned it, and I'm teaching him the eagle. I gave it to him the way my father gave it to me, by walking it together until he could do it blind. It isn't the seventh generation of my family. It's the seventh generation of the route, and that's what matters. Jakshy, that's good.

moments.prompt: He won't talk about anything until you've had tea with him.

options.reply: Jakshy, that's good. Drink, and then we'll walk.
Then you're not ready to walk with me. Come back when you can sit.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to help him clear the third leg of his route.

options.reply: Good, we leave at first light, and you step where I step.

options.text: Why does the route matter so much?
options.reply: Because a route is how the dead walk with you. My father is on every step of mine.

lines.bored_warning: We walk the same circle and kill the same things. A herder doesn't graze one field to dirt, so let's move on.
lines.leaving_good: Good walking, all of it. I'll go back to the pasture now, Jeldyz misses the wind. Come and drink tea when you want me.
lines.leaving_bored: Back to the pasture for me. You're grazing one field to dirt here, and I won't do it.
lines.after_wipe: Sit down, everybody, and breathe. Then we look at where the ground lied to us.
lines.wipe_warning: We fall here too often. I'll walk this one to the end with you, and then the mountains for a while.
lines.wipe_leave: It's finished, so I'm going home to the pasture. Come and find me when you've learned to read this place.
lines.zone_warning: This ground is too high for us. Even the eagle wouldn't fly here. We should go back down.
lines.zone_leave: The ground was too high, like I said. I'll be on the pasture in Eastern Hillsbrad, drinking tea.
lines.gear_refuse: No, I keep my things. We haven't shared enough tea yet.
lines.gear_taken: You can take it. I've walked the mountains with less.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing a piece, and the cold finds the gap every night.
lines.gear_upgrade: This is good work. Rakhmat, thank you.
lines.back: Jeldyz is fat and happy, and so am I. Where do we walk?
lines.send_word: Bakyt has sent word from Eastern Hillsbrad. The herds are settled and he's ready to walk with you again.
lines.walkout_talk: My father wouldn't have walked off like I did. Sit, drink tea, and I'll tell you why. Then it's your turn.
lines.neglect: You've been gone a long time. I kept tea warm anyway, so sit.
lines.asked_to_stay: Jakshy, one more walk. Then the pasture.
lines.on_break: Bakyt is back on the high pasture in Eastern Hillsbrad. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: My name's Bashir, and I hunt corruption. I'll tell you everything I find, plainly. I work slowly, and I won't be hurried. If you can accept that, we'll get on.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Nablus. My grandfather and my father cut stone in the same yard, and I learned it at twelve. Twenty-two years of walls, old and new. You snap a chalk line across the block before you cut, so the cut runs true. I still do it, at every door. I know I do it.
stages.companion: I've got a daughter, Rana. She was nineteen, at university in Birzeit. When all this happened I went looking for her at once, and I didn't stop for eleven months. Four hubs, on foot, through country that kills people, and I found nothing. I came back and started this work. I keep a list of places I haven't searched. It's getting shorter.
stages.friend: My wife was Samira. She died bearing our second child, and the child died too, when Rana was three. I raised Rana alone, strictly, and I wanted her to be a doctor or a teacher. There are three places left on my list, the hardest, through corrupted country. I'd like you to come with me to the end of it.
stages.sworn: There was no sign of her, not at any of the three. At the last, a camp of engineers building a bridge, the foreman had never heard of her. So I said it out loud to you, at last. I was pleased she chose engineering, and proud, and she'd be good at it. Then I helped them build the bridge, stone by stone, correctly. I've started a new list. Every bridge being built, anywhere. If she's alive, she's building one.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to come with him to the last places on his list.

options.text: To the end of the list, together.
options.reply: Thank you. We'll go slowly, and correctly, and we'll look properly.

options.text: What happens when the list runs out?
options.reply: I don't know. That's why I've been walking slowly.

moments.prompt: After the wipe he reports, flatly, what went wrong.
moments.line: We went against the grain. This isn't how it's done. We'll start again from the first stone.

options.reply: Good, slowly, then, and you'll see it.

options.text: We haven't got time for slow.
options.reply: Then you'll spend it on wipes instead.

lines.bored_warning: We repeat the same work for no reason. I don't mind slow, but I mind pointless, so let's go where we're needed.
lines.leaving_good: Good work, and done correctly. I'll be at the Drowned Shrine if you need me.
lines.leaving_bored: This isn't useful, and the corruption doesn't wait. I'm going back to the Shrine.
lines.after_wipe: We went against the grain. We'll start again, slowly.
lines.wipe_warning: Again and again we fail here, and it's the same mistake. When this is done, I need some days at the Shrine.
lines.wipe_leave: It's finished, and I'm going back to the Shrine. Come when you're ready to work properly.
lines.zone_warning: I'll say it plainly. We shouldn't be here, and every step further makes it worse.
lines.zone_leave: I told you plainly, and you went on anyway. I'll be at the Drowned Shrine.
lines.gear_refuse: No, that stays with me. I haven't known you long enough.
lines.gear_taken: If you need it, take it. I'll work without it, slowly.
lines.gear_short: I still haven't got a replacement for that piece. Consider it reported.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's well made, and I know good work. Thank you.
lines.back: The Shrine is holding without me for now. Tell me the job.
lines.send_word: Bashir has sent word from the Drowned Shrine. He's ready to come out again.
lines.walkout_talk: There's a reason I went, and you'll hear all of it. Then you'll tell me yours, and we'll start again.
lines.neglect: You've been gone a long time. I kept working, as I always do.
lines.asked_to_stay: Very well, one more, yalla.
lines.on_break: Bashir is back at the Drowned Shrine, at the edge of the corruption. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We said we'd do it, and we've left it. This isn't how it's done.

stages.stranger: I'm Berat, and I'm a dentist, so I'm the best healer you'll ever meet for small careful work. Before we go anywhere, tell me what you did before all this. I ask everybody. I'll remember, I promise.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Izmir, from Karşıyaka on the north side of the bay. Three generations of Yilmazes in one building on four floors, and every one of them talking at the same time. My father sold carpets, my mother ran everything, and I've got three older brothers, all louder than me. I was the first to go to university. My grandmother told the whole street.
stages.companion: I had my own surgery for eleven months, abi. My name on the door and a loan with thirty years left. I was in the middle of a filling when it happened and I landed near Brill with this mirror behind my ear. My whole family was in Izmir, all of them. I haven't found one. I say I will. I say it every day, because if I stop saying it I don't know what happens.
stages.friend: There was a girl, Elif. My mother very much wanted me to marry her, and I was getting used to the idea. I think about how she laughed at my jokes even when they were bad, which was always. And I've got this list, every medic from Earth I've ever met. If anything bad ever happens somewhere, I can send for help that nobody else knows exists. I think one day it'll matter.
stages.sworn: They were at the Crossroads the whole time, canım. A carpet stall and a tea house, and the noise when I walked in brought the orc guards running. My mother slapped me for taking so long and then wouldn't let go. My grandmother told the entire market I'm a doctor. One of my brothers didn't make it, and my father's older. But I've got a surgery at the Crossroads with my name on the door, and every Sunday they all come and eat there.

moments.prompt: After the wipe he's grinning, but his hands are shaking a little.
moments.line: Okay, okay, good news, everyone still has all their teeth. Bad news is everything else. Let me look at you.

options.text: You can stop joking for a minute, you know.
options.reply: Can I really? Okay then, that was frightening, abi. Give me a second.
That's the spirit! I'll think of a better joke for next time.

moments.prompt: He's just shown you his list of medics.

options.text: Nobody else would have thought of this.
options.reply: Somebody had to, and I'm very nosy. It's the same thing.

options.text: Is your family's doctor on it?
options.reply: I check, every time I add a name. Not yet, abi.

lines.bored_warning: Abi, we've seen the same faces for days and none of them were people. I need somebody new to talk to.
lines.leaving_good: Six new names for my list! I'm off to Brill to write them up, and you can come and hear a joke.
lines.leaving_bored: Back to Brill for me. Out here it's the same thing every day, and I'd rather be fixing arms on a busy road.
lines.after_wipe: Everybody still has all their teeth, so that's something. Come here, let me look at you all.
lines.wipe_warning: We've died in here so often my jokes have stopped landing, and that's never happened before. One more run, then I need a rest.
lines.wipe_leave: I'll walk out with you, but I'm going back to Brill for a while. I need to be somewhere loud and safe.
lines.zone_warning: Abi, everything out here is bigger than us. I can fix a lot, but I can't fix being eaten.
lines.zone_leave: It's too dangerous out there for me right now, abi. I'll be in Brill, above the inn.
lines.gear_refuse: Ah, no, I'd like to keep that one. When you know how I take my tea, we'll talk.
lines.gear_taken: Oh, all right, have it. I'll be fine, and I'll complain about it in a funny way.
lines.gear_short: My arm's noticed that missing piece, abi, even if you haven't.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, this is beautiful! Thank you, canım. Now I owe you a free check-up.
lines.back: Four new names on my list since I saw you! Where are we off to?
lines.send_word: Berat has sent word from Brill. He's got new names for his list and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: Abi, I'm never angry, so you know it was bad when I went. Sit down and I'll explain without a single joke.
lines.neglect: Abi, you came back! I've been telling strangers about you so they'd know you were real.
lines.asked_to_stay: I'll stay, abi, as long as I'm telling the jokes.
lines.on_break: Berat is back in Brill, on whichever road is busiest. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Callum, mate, and I'm a venomancer, so I've been bitten by most things and I'm fine. I'll stand in front and take the bites for you. Don't worry about the scorpion, she's friendly.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Brisbane. Dad was an electrician, Mum ran a childcare centre, and I spent my whole childhood catching lizards in the backyard. Then sixteen years at a reptile sanctuary up in the hinterland. Taipans, death adders, crocs, and school groups who all asked the same question about the same snake.
stages.companion: I've been bitten a lot, but there was one taipan, about ten years ago, that nearly did me. Three days in hospital. I went straight back to work after, and my sister Kirsty still hasn't forgiven me. She went into law and can't believe what I do for a living. I was mid-feed in the snake house when it happened, and I landed in the Barrens with my hook in my hand.
stages.friend: I had a dog, a blue heeler called Biscuit. Best mate I ever had, honestly, and I had to leave her behind. I miss her more than I miss most people, and I know how that sounds. I've been further into the Wailing Caverns than nearly anyone. I want to go all the way down, mate, right to the bottom, and meet whatever lives there. Will you come?
stages.sworn: It was old, mate, and enormous, and the dream-sickness had got right into it. It couldn't be fixed. It was suffering, and it'd have killed everyone who came down. So you held it, and I did it quickly, the way I'd do it for an animal at the sanctuary that couldn't be saved. I sat with it for an hour after and talked to it. Most interesting thing I've ever met, and I'm the one who had to kill it.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to come to the bottom of the Wailing Caverns with him.

options.text: I'm in. Let's go and meet it.
options.reply: You're a legend. Bring some antivenom. Actually, don't bother, I'm the antivenom.

options.text: Why do you want to get bitten so badly?
options.reply: It's not the bite, mate. It's the meeting. The bite's just how they say hello.

moments.prompt: After the wipe he's gone quiet and quick, which is how you know he's worried.
moments.line: Right, that's not a no worries situation. Everyone stay still while I look at you.

options.reply: Good on you. I'll have you patched up in a minute, mate.

options.text: It's fine, we'll just go again.
options.reply: It's not fine, mate. Sit down for a sec.

lines.bored_warning: Mate, we've been killing the same boring stuff for ages and none of it's venomous. Can we go somewhere with teeth?
lines.leaving_good: What a ripper of a trip. I'm heading back to the Southern Barrens to check on my jars. Drop in whenever, mate.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm off back to my hut. Nothing out here's worth the bother, and my scorpions need feeding.
lines.after_wipe: Okay, that's not a no worries situation. Everyone stay still and let me look at you.
lines.wipe_warning: Mate, I've been taken down more times today than in sixteen years with crocs. Get me through this one and then I'm having a break.
lines.wipe_leave: I stuck it out, but I'm heading home now. I'll be in the Southern Barrens with my jars.
lines.zone_warning: Mate, everything out here is bigger and meaner than us, and it's not even venomous. Let's pick a fight we can actually win.
lines.zone_leave: Nah, I'm done for now, it's too much out there. You'll find me in the Southern Barrens.
lines.gear_refuse: Nah, that's mine, mate. We'll talk about it when I know you a bit better.
lines.gear_taken: No worries, take it. I've got thick skin, literally.
lines.gear_short: I'm still a piece short, mate. I'll live, but it'd be nice.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's beautiful, mate. Cheers, I owe you one.
lines.back: The scorpions say hi, mate. Where are we headed?
lines.send_word: Callum has sent word from the Southern Barrens. His jars are full and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: Mate, I don't usually storm off. Sit down, I'll explain, and then you have a go.
lines.neglect: Mate, you're alive! I was half expecting to hear something finally bit you that you couldn't handle.
lines.asked_to_stay: Yeah, no worries, one more. Then I've got scorpions to feed.
lines.on_break: Callum is back in his hut in the Southern Barrens, with his jars. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Camila, a venomancer. Stand still, please, there's a scorpid by your boot. If anyone gets poisoned, tell me straight away. I'm good at that part.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Durango, in Mexico, where scorpions come into the houses every summer and every kid shakes out their shoes. My dad drove a truck and my mum had a little shop. I worked seven years in an antivenom lab, milking scorpions with tweezers. Ten thousand of them, and the venom turned into antivenom that saved kids all over the country.
stages.companion: My little sister Daniela called me every night to complain about boys, and I listened to every word. She's six years younger, and loud where I'm quiet. I was milking a scorpion in the lab when it happened, and I landed in Tanaris with my safety glasses in my hair. I haven't found her or my parents. Ni modo, I keep looking.
stages.friend: Once the hospital next door brought in a boy, six years old, stung by a bark scorpion. I ran over with a batch I'd made that week, and he lived. I still see his face. That's why I do this. And now there's a new giant scorpid out of the deep sand whose sting kills in an hour, and there's no antivenom. I need one alive. That's much harder than dead.
stages.sworn: At the camp there was a young woman nursing the stung and shouting at everybody and organising everything, and it was Daniela. She's been nursing in the Tanaris camps for two years and looking for me on every list. She took one look at the antivenom and said, of course it's you. We saved everyone. That night she complained about a goblin she's seeing for two hours, and I listened to every word.

moments.prompt: She tells you, very calmly, that there's a scorpid on your arm.

options.reply: Good, very good. There, she's gone. You'd have made a decent lab tech.
Órale, don't do that. She was just passing through.

moments.prompt: She's asked you to help her bring the giant scorpid back alive.

options.text: Alive it is. Show me how.
options.reply: Neta, you'll help? Okay, then, stand where I tell you, and don't move when it looks at you.
Dead doesn't make venom. Alive saves the camp.

lines.bored_warning: I haven't seen a single new scorpid in days. There must be something interesting in the sand somewhere else.
lines.leaving_good: Nobody got stung, so I'm happy. I'm off to my rock in Tanaris to sort my antivenoms, and stand still when you visit.
lines.leaving_bored: Nothing out here needs me, and my antivenoms need sorting. I'll be in Tanaris.
lines.after_wipe: Okay, nobody move until I check if anyone's been poisoned.
lines.wipe_warning: Every time we die in here I count it, and I don't like the number. After this run I need some quiet on my rock.
lines.wipe_leave: That's the run done. I'm going home to Tanaris for a while, to be quiet.
lines.zone_warning: Stop there, please. I can't make antivenom for everything out here, and I don't want to try. We should go back.
lines.zone_leave: Too dangerous out there, like I said. I'll be on my rock in Northern Tanaris.
lines.gear_refuse: Not yet, sorry. Maybe later, when I know you.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, ni modo, I'll manage.
lines.gear_short: That piece is still missing, by the way. I'm not upset about it.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's good work, gracias.
lines.back: I've got seven antivenoms now, all labelled. What's the job?
lines.send_word: Camila has sent word from Northern Tanaris. Her antivenoms are sorted and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I went off angry, and I want to explain it quietly. After that I'll listen to you.
lines.neglect: You came back. I sat very still the whole time, in case you were nearby.
lines.asked_to_stay: Okay, I'll stay for one more. My rock isn't going anywhere.
lines.on_break: Camila is back on her rock in Northern Tanaris, watching the sand. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Camille, and I'm fast, and I map things. I go first, I don't wait for slow people, and I don't talk about feelings, yes? If that's a problem, find another ranger.
stages.acquaintance: Lyon, from Villeurbanne just outside. Papa was a postman and Maman cleaned at a hospital. I was a bike courier for nine years, and I fixed everybody's bikes because nobody else could do it properly. I could cross the whole city in twenty-two minutes. I'm still faster than anyone here, by the way.
stages.companion: There was Margaux, a pastry chef, for three years. Her mornings started when my shifts ended, and it went badly at the end, mostly because I wouldn't talk about anything. I know that now. I was in bed when all this happened, and I landed in the Barrens in my pyjamas with this wrench on my keyring. Don't laugh, everybody laughs.
stages.friend: My little brother Théo rode for the same company. That morning he was on the Part-Dieu road, and it should have been me, because I swapped the shift so I could sleep in. I think he's dead, on my road. I've never looked on the lists, because I don't want to see it written down. Now a goblin's complaining about a French courier who reads every message before he takes it. Come with me, yes? Don't say anything.
stages.sworn: It was Théo, alive, older, and just as annoying as before. He's been reading every message for three years for exactly the same reason I do. I told him about the swapped shift, and he laughed at me and said he'd always have taken Part-Dieu because it's the best road. We argued about the fastest route to the Crossroads the whole way back. If you tell anyone I was smiling, I'll deny it.

moments.prompt: At the end of her first trip with you, she's already got her bag on.
moments.line: Right, that was fine, I'm off. I've got roads to map, yes?

options.reply: Obviously you're faster with me. Fine, I'll stay, but I'm still going first.
Yes, see you. Try not to get lost without me.

moments.prompt: She's just told you about the swapped shift.

options.text: Say nothing, and walk next to her.
options.reply: Merci, that's exactly right. Allez, let's go.
I said don't say anything, yes? That included that.

lines.bored_warning: We've been in this same boring field for days, yes? I'm going to die of slowness. Let's go somewhere I haven't mapped.
lines.leaving_good: Not bad, actually, and I almost enjoyed it. I'm going back to the Caverns to finish a map. Find me there, if you can find it.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm off now. This is the same loop again and again, and I don't do loops.
lines.after_wipe: Putain, that was slow. Next time, faster, and somebody watch the left side.
lines.wipe_warning: Dying is boring, and we keep doing it. I'll finish this, then I'm gone for a bit, yes?
lines.wipe_leave: I finished it, like I said. Now I'm off to my maps, and you can come back when you've learned to move.
lines.zone_warning: Even I can't outrun all of that, yes? Turn around and let's be sensible for once.
lines.zone_leave: You didn't listen, so I'm leaving, yes? I'll be at the Wailing Caverns.
lines.gear_refuse: Non, that's mine. Ask me again in about a year.
lines.gear_taken: Fine, take it, but I'm going to complain about it the whole way.
lines.gear_short: I'm mentioning that missing piece so you can feel bad, yes?
lines.gear_upgrade: Merci, that's actually decent. Don't make it weird.
lines.back: Three more tunnels mapped while you were dawdling. Allez, let's go.
lines.send_word: Camille has sent word from the Wailing Caverns. Her maps are done for now and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: Yes, I went, and I'm not sorry, but you'll get the reason, quickly. Then you talk, and then we go.
lines.neglect: Oh, there you are. I'd assumed you'd got lost. You should have a map, I've got lots.
lines.asked_to_stay: Fine, one more, but I'm going first.
lines.on_break: Camille is back at the Wailing Caverns, mapping. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We left somebody waiting, yes? I hate that. In my job you deliver, always.

stages.stranger: I'm Carolina, and I'm a shaman, and before that I was a river pilot. I'm happiest near water and I get grumpy underground, so now you know. Calma, we'll get on fine.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Manaus, in Brazil, where the Rio Negro meets the Amazon and the two waters run side by side for miles without mixing. I piloted cargo boats for twelve years. The captains didn't trust a woman at first, and after the first season they did, because a channel that was deep in March would ground you in September and I always knew.
stages.companion: My grandfather, Seu Raimundo, taught me the river. I spent my whole childhood on his boats. He died when I was thirty and I scattered his ashes where the waters meet. This was his compass. I never used it on the river, I just carried it, and it was in my pocket when I landed here in the shallows. My mother and my little brother were in Manaus. I think about them on the water every morning, and then I let it go downstream.
stages.friend: I was married to Joana, a teacher, for five years. We split up because I was on the river three weeks in four, and we stayed friends. We had lunch every month. I miss those lunches more than I expected to. And I want something I've never wanted before, meu bem. I want to stay in one place, if it's the right place. There's a river in Ashenvale that nobody's ever run properly. I'd like you to come and see it with me.
stages.sworn: The river let me on. You saw it, the whole stretch nobody's ever run, and I laughed the entire way down. I've built a house on the bank, and the Darkspear boy from the Isles has come to be my apprentice, and he's getting it. I'll still be learning this river in twenty years. That's the best thing anyone's ever told me, and I'm the one who said it.

moments.prompt: After the wipe she sits down where she is and laughs, a bit shakily.
moments.line: Okay, everybody breathe. We went against the current in there, that's all. We'll find the right line next time.

options.text: Show us the right line, then.
options.reply: That's the spirit. Watch where I go, and go there too.
Nossa, everything's a river. You'll see it soon.

stages.stranger: Hermano, I'm Cristóbal! I'm a firefighter, or I was, and now the fire lives inside me, which is very funny if you think about it. I go in first and I come out last, that's the rule.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Valparaíso, from the hills above the port, hermano. My father left when I was four, and my mother cleaned offices and raised me alone, and sent me off every morning with empanadas. I joined the forest fire brigade at twenty-three. Twelve years in the hills, on a motorbike that broke down every week, and I danced cueca very badly at every fiesta.
stages.companion: In 2024 the hills above my mother's house burned, and I spent four days on the line while the city burned below us. Her house was still standing when I came down. I'll never forget that. My mother is Inés. I haven't found her, so I write her a letter every week and I keep them all, in a sack, cachai.
stages.friend: On my first day here I landed in the middle of a grass fire in the Barrens. There were other people in it, people from Earth, and I was the only one who walked out. I've never stopped thinking about them. That's why I train the young tauren to cut breaks. The dry season's coming early this year, hermano, and something big is going to come at Taurajo. I need you with me on the line.
stages.sworn: The line held, and the kids held it without me for the last hour while I was pulling people out. They did it, not me. And then a letter came from across the sea. My mother's alive! She heard there's a crazy Chilean fighting fires in the Barrens and she knew it was me, and she told me to be careful. I sent her all the letters at once, three years of them, in a sack. She's going to be reading for a month.

stages.stranger: I'm Dan, and I go first and I stand in front, and you lot get on with it behind me. Don't thank me, it's the job and somebody has to have it.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Sheffield, Attercliffe. My dad came over from Enugu in the sixties and worked the steel for thirty years, and my mum was a dinner lady from Rotherham. I went on the floor at eighteen, same plant as him. Twenty-two years on a four-man crew. Me, Gaz, Little Mick and Pete. We went for a pint every Friday for nine years straight.
stages.companion: I've got a daughter, Jade. She's twenty-eight, a paramedic, in Leeds. Married a lad called Craig Dawson the year before all this, so she's a Dawson on the lists now. I've been through the D's at the hub about forty times. I'd just started driving a forklift in a warehouse when it happened, so I landed in Durotar in a hi-vis vest, like a right lemon.
stages.friend: The plant shut in 2019. I was out of work four years after. Stopped going out, stopped answering the phone, spent most of it on the sofa. Jade came round every Sunday and made me eat. She's the reason I got through it and I've never told her. So I want to find her and tell her. Will you come with me round the lists? Every hub we can get to.

I've left a note at every hub, under both names. I've stopped trying to build a crew out of whoever's in the tavern, because I've got one. It's this lot. I still check the D's, mind.

stages.stranger: I'm Delroy, and I brew. Sit down, drink this, and don't ask what's in it. You wouldn't thank me, and you'll feel better in a minute.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Kingston, near Spanish Town Road. My mother sold in the market and my father worked the docks. I went into a bakery at twenty-two and stayed thirty-one years, nights, in at eleven and out at seven. I fed a whole city its breakfast, and not one of them ever asked what was in the bread.
stages.companion: My wife was Marcia. The cancer took her when I was forty-six. I kept working nights after, because the nights were when I missed her least. I was pulling the first loaves at four in the morning when all this happened, which is the only reason I wasn't asleep. My son Andre's a sailor, on cargo ships. If anyone landed near water, it's him.
stages.friend: My daughter Shanice is a nurse, and she's got a likkle girl, Kezia, who was five and called me Grandy. I ask every ship that ties up for three names, Andre, Shanice and Kezia Beckford, and in three years I've had one maybe. A sailor said a Jamaican called Beckford was crewing a ship out of Ratchet. Help me find that ship, nuh?
stages.sworn: Andre was in the hold, pressed by the Bloodsail, and he lifted me clean off the deck. Then he told me Shanice and Kezia are alive, in a camp of Jamaicans near Ratchet. Kezia's eight now. She looked at me a long time, and then she said Grandy and ran at me. I've built an oven near the camp, and she's my apprentice, though she's mostly interested in the eating. Mi soon come, they say, and I came.

stages.stranger: I'm Diego, and I fix things, anything, and if it's broken I'll hear what's wrong with it before you finish telling me. I used to fix phones, but I'm not fussy, my friend. If it has a gear in it, give it to me.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Maracaibo, in Venezuela. I started at a phone kiosk in a mall when I was fifteen, and the power went off twice a day there, so everybody learned to work in the dark. After a year people queued for me by name. I'm the youngest of five and the only boy, and my sisters all left the country, one by one, in different directions.
stages.companion: I was the one who stayed. My mother got sick and somebody had to look after her, so for four years it was the kiosk all day and her all night. She died when I was twenty-two, eight months before all this. So when I landed in Deathknell there was nobody left at home for me to lose. A goblin gave me a broken valve to see what I'd do, I fixed it, and I've been paid in parts ever since.

stages.stranger: I'm Driss, a shaman, and before that a desert guide. Drink some water first, please, and then we'll talk. I never let anybody in my care run short of water.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Zagora, in Morocco, at the edge of the Sahara. My father and grandfather guided caravans across the desert, and I learned the routes on a camel before I could read. When the tourists came I guided them too, first on camels and later in two old Land Cruisers I kept running with my own hands, for twenty-eight years.
stages.companion: I was under a truck in the desert fixing an axle with this wrench when it happened, and I landed on the salt flats here with it still in my hand. I asked the land for permission in my own language, and something answered. My wife is Khadija. We have four children. Youssef, Amina and Hamza are grown. Nour was nine.
stages.friend: Nour came long after the others, and she was the light of our house. She'd be twelve now. I tell stories about her by the fire because if I stop telling them I'm afraid I'll forget her laugh. The last stretch of my summer route needs water, and there's none on any map. I think there's a spring under the salt. Will you help me find it, inshallah?
stages.sworn: On the second night of the first summer crossing, I heard a girl laughing at the back of the caravan, and I knew the laugh. It was Nour, twelve now, and Khadija with her. They'd been waiting in a Moroccan camp in Tanaris for two years, unable to cross the Flats in summer. My route brought them. I carried her the rest of the way on my shoulders, though she says she's too old. That night I made mint tea for everybody.

stages.stranger: I'm Eino, and I hit things with an axe. I don't talk much. That's not because I don't like you, it's just how I am.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Lapland, outside Kittilä, above the Arctic Circle. My family cut and planted the same forest for four generations. I felled timber for twenty-six years, chainsaw first, then a harvester. Six months of dark every winter. I liked it, very much.
stages.companion: I was in my harvester in a winter forest when it happened, and I landed here in the heat in my thermal gear. This tape on my arm marks trees that stay standing. I work for goblins now, cutting jungle down, and I know what that says about me. So I plant one for every one I cut, at night, where nobody sees.
stages.friend: My father left our forest to me and my brother Juha. Juha wanted to sell it to a company that would clear it. I said no. He sold his half anyway, and I watched it come down in one winter. We haven't spoken since. Now the goblins want to clear a huge stretch of old jungle, and I'm going to argue with the foreman. Come with me. I'm bad at arguing.
stages.sworn: The foreman was Juha. Two years running clear-cuts for the goblins, and I didn't know. Afterwards he said he was wrong, at home and here. I said I was too stubborn to listen. That's all either of us said. He's changed the plan to selective felling, the way our father did it. Then we sat in my sauna together for three hours without a word, and jumped in the river. Best conversation we've ever had.
