lines.wipe_warning: My crow's started hiding whenever we die, and I don't blame it. I'll finish this run, but I need a few days off after.
lines.wipe_leave: That's over, thank goodness. I'll be on the Black Strand for a while, drawing something cheerful.
lines.zone_warning: Even my crow's nervous, and it's already dead. Let's go back.
lines.zone_leave: Even my crow said no, and it never says no. I'll be on the Black Strand.
lines.gear_refuse: Na, that's mine. Give me a few more weeks of you first.
lines.gear_taken: Go on, then. I'll be fine without it.
lines.gear_short: That missing piece is starting to annoy me, just so you know.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's gorgeous. Köszönöm, thank you.
lines.back: My crow's learned a new hop! Shall I show you on the way?
lines.send_word: Réka has sent word from the Black Strand. Her crow's restless and so is she.
lines.walkout_talk: I stormed off, and I'd like to explain properly. After that you get your turn.
lines.neglect: Finally, you're back! My crow kept looking for you, and so did I.
lines.asked_to_stay: Jó, one more. Then I sketch.
lines.on_break: Réka is back on the Black Strand with her crow. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Rhys, and this is Tegan. Keep your voice down near the trees, would you? She hunts better when nobody's chattering, and she's watching you, so be nice.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Brecon, in the Beacons, in Wales. I was a falconer at a centre outside town, weddings in summer and school visits in winter, mostly keeping a bird calm in front of two hundred people in hats. Tegan's a Harris's hawk. She's been mine seven years, and she was on my glove the evening it all happened, so she came with me.
stages.companion: My dad farmed, and he died when I was eleven. My mam took a job running the café at the falconry centre so we'd manage, and I spent every day after school with the birds. I was flying hawks by fourteen. Everything good I've got came out of that. Tegan found her first hare here inside a week, and I thought, well, if she can, I can.
stages.friend: My mam's name is Gwen. She called every bird at the centre by the wrong name on purpose, and she called Tegan the chicken. I don't know if Brecon's anywhere in this world, cariad. A Welsh trader says there's a camp of people from the Beacons across the mountains. I'd like to go, and Tegan likes you, so I'd like you to come.
stages.sworn: The camp was empty, a long time empty, no list and no names. But by the gate somebody had carved a hawk into a post, rough, and the word Gwen. I don't know if it was my mam, or someone with the same name. I've decided it was her, and she's somewhere, and she'd want me to keep flying. I carved a hawk and my name under it. The Sun Rock boy's my apprentice now.

moments.prompt: Tegan looks you over from his glove before he'll say yes.

options.text: Stand still and let her look.
options.reply: There, she likes you. Tidy, I'll get my things.
Duw, no, she's had enough of you for today. Come back tomorrow, slower.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to come to the camp from the Beacons.

options.reply: Diolch, thank you. Tegan will scout ahead, she loves a long walk.
Then it's empty, and I'll know. Not knowing is heavier, mind.

lines.bored_warning: We've been round this same patch for days and Tegan's bored, and when she's bored she sulks. Somewhere new, please.
lines.leaving_good: That was lovely, thank you. I'm taking Tegan back to the ridges in Stonetalon for a bit. Say hello if you're passing.
lines.leaving_bored: There's nothing out here for her to hunt but the same old things. We're going back to Stonetalon.
lines.after_wipe: Is everybody all right? Tegan's fine, she went up a tree, the clever girl.
lines.wipe_warning: Tegan doesn't like the dark, and she likes watching us die even less. After this one she needs some sky, and so do I.
lines.wipe_leave: That's the end of it, and Tegan needs open air, so we're going back to Stonetalon.
lines.zone_warning: Tegan knows we're outmatched, look at her feathers. Let's back away slowly.
lines.zone_leave: Tegan won't hunt out there, and I trust her. We'll be on the western ridges in Stonetalon.
lines.gear_refuse: I'd rather keep that, if it's all the same. Tegan doesn't know you well enough yet either.
lines.gear_taken: That's fine, take it. Tegan doesn't care what I wear.
lines.gear_short: Tegan's noticed I'm a piece short, mind, and she judges.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's tidy, that is. Diolch, thank you.
lines.back: We're back, me and Tegan, and she's caught a lot of hares. She's ready if you are.
lines.send_word: Rhys has sent word from Stonetalon West. He and Tegan are ready to come out again.
lines.walkout_talk: I'm not proud of how I left. Sit down, quietly, Tegan's watching, and I'll tell you why.
lines.neglect: Look, Tegan, it's them. She kept looking for you on the road, and so did I, a bit.
lines.asked_to_stay: Go on, then, one more, Tegan's game.
lines.on_break: Rhys is back on the western ridges of Stonetalon with Tegan. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Rosa, and I hunt. I'll tell you what the animals out here are about to do before they do it, and you'll listen, because I'm usually right. I don't kill things for nothing, so don't ask me to.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Madrid, from Lavapiés. My dad drove a bus and my mum did hair. I spent every summer at my grandparents' farm in Extremadura watching eagles, and at ten I decided I was going to Africa. I went to Tanzania at twenty-six for a six-month research job and stayed eight years, guiding out of Arusha.
stages.companion: My dad died when I was thirty-one. My mum sold the flat in Madrid and moved to Arusha to be near me, and opened a little salon for the expats. I pretended to be annoyed and I was very glad. Arusha came down on the far side of the mountains from here. I landed in the Barrens with my binoculars and nothing else, and then I spent a year being outclassed by pigs.
stages.friend: I've never stayed with anyone long. Wanjiru, a Kenyan bush pilot, and we split over who was going to move. Before her there was Bram, a Dutch photographer, and that ended because he talked in the hide. I'd rather sit still in the dark than talk about any of it. There's a hyena matriarch on the Crossroads road who's cleverer than every caravan master put together. I'd like your help to deal with her, properly.
stages.sworn: I didn't shoot her. She was only hungry, and hunger isn't personal. I drove the pack off the road for good with fire and noise in the right places, and the caravan masters are furious about the bounty. Then I walked to Ratchet, took my boots off, and walked into the sea for the first time in my life. I laughed like an idiot. I'm owed one more thing now, the far side of the mountain, and I'll get there.

moments.prompt: She's told you about the hyena matriarch on the Crossroads road.

options.reply: Sawa, we'll do it. My way means waiting, a lot of waiting, pole pole.

options.text: There's a bounty on her. Easy money.
options.reply: That's exactly the kind of thinking I'm trying to get away from.

moments.prompt: After the wipe, she's furious, mostly with herself.
moments.line: I saw that pack shift and I read it wrong. That's on me, and I hate it.

options.text: You'll read it right next time.
options.reply: I will, because I'm not making that mistake twice.
Not me, not usually, anyway.

lines.bored_warning: We've been killing the same animals in the same place for no reason. I don't do that. Find us somewhere new or I'm going back to my road.
lines.leaving_good: Good hunting, and nothing killed for nothing. I'll be out in the Barrens watching my hyenas for a while.
lines.leaving_bored: This is just killing for the sake of it, and I've got no patience for that. I'm going back to the Barrens.
lines.after_wipe: Right, that went badly. Let's work out what we missed before anyone tries anything clever.
lines.wipe_warning: This place has us for lunch every time. One more, and then I want to be somewhere I can see the horizon.
lines.wipe_leave: We're done here. I'll be in the Barrens, and you can find me when you've learned to read a trail.
lines.zone_warning: Everything out here is bigger, faster and cleverer than us, and we'd be the ones getting hunted. Let's get out of here.
lines.zone_leave: Out there we're the prey, and I'm nobody's prey. I'll be on the Crossroads road.
lines.gear_refuse: You'll get that when I trust you, and not before.
lines.gear_taken: Fine, take it. I've managed with worse in worse places.
lines.gear_short: Still short a piece. I notice everything out here, including that.
lines.gear_upgrade: Decent of you, that. Good kit, thanks.
lines.back: The hyenas have been very well behaved. What are we hunting?
lines.send_word: Rosa has sent word from the Central Barrens. Her road's quiet and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: You'll hear why I went, plainly. Then you can tell me I'm wrong and we'll see.
lines.neglect: Oh, there you are. I'd assumed something ate you. Glad it didn't.
lines.asked_to_stay: I'll stay, but I'm choosing where we sleep.
lines.on_break: Rosa is back on the Crossroads road in the Central Barrens. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Rui, and I'm sorry, I heal people, but please don't ask me how. I'll tell you what it does. The rest I can't say. Desculpa, I know that's strange.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Peniche, a fishing town on the Portuguese coast. My father fished, and he drowned when I was fourteen. At sixteen I went to sea myself, to send money home. Twenty years on the sardine boats, nights out and mornings in, and the co-operative went from forty boats to nine. I mended nets in the evenings with this needle. He carved it.
stages.companion: I landed on the rocks on the Tanaris coast, alone, with my leg broken, in the dark. Something offered to help me, and I said yes, and it's been with me ever since. It mended my leg. It heals you now. It frightens me every day. I sleep by the fire because in the dark it's louder. I'm sorry, I shouldn't have said that much.
stages.friend: My mother and my sisters, Inês and Sofia, are in Peniche, or they were. I sent money every week for twenty years. I think about the money more than I think about them, and I'm ashamed of that. And I want out of this thing, more than anything. A Darkspear sea-witch says there's an old rite. You row out into a storm and give it to the sea. Will you help me build a boat?
stages.sworn: I gave it to the sea, and the sea took it, and then the sea gave me back. I can't heal the way I could, and I really don't care. I slept away from the fire last night, in the dark, for the first time in three years. So I can tell you what it was now, because it's gone. It was hungry, and it was patient, and it was always very polite. Obrigado, thank you for standing on the shore.

moments.prompt: He's just healed you, and he's waiting to see if you'll ask how.

options.reply: Obrigado, thank you. You don't know how much that means.
I'm sorry, I can't tell you. Please don't ask me again.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to help build the boat for the rite.

options.text: We'll build it the Peniche way.
options.reply: Pois, yes, the old way. My father would have liked that.

options.text: What if the sea takes you too?
options.reply: Then it takes me. I'd still rather go out there than keep this.

lines.bored_warning: Sorry, but I don't think anyone needs me out here. Could we go somewhere useful? Only if you want.
lines.leaving_good: Thank you for letting me come. I'll be on the coast for a while, near the sea.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm sorry, I'm going back to the Lashings. I don't think I'm helping out here.
lines.after_wipe: I'm sorry, I'm sorry. Let me heal everyone. Please hold still.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here, and it gets louder when we do. One more run, please, and then the sea.
lines.wipe_leave: That's done, and I'm sorry, but I need the coast for a while.
lines.zone_warning: I'm sorry, I'm frightened, and I think we should go back before it's too late.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here, I'm sorry. I'll be at the Lashings, on the coast.
lines.gear_refuse: I'm sorry, I'd like to keep that. I hope that's all right.
lines.gear_taken: Of course, take it, desculpa. I didn't deserve it anyway.
lines.gear_short: I'm sorry to mention it, but I'm still missing that piece.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's very kind. Obrigado, I mean it.
lines.back: I've been by the sea, so I feel better. Sorry, I'm ready now, if you still want me.
lines.send_word: Rui has sent word from the Lashings. He's ready to come out again, if you'll have him.
lines.walkout_talk: I'm sorry I left like that. I'd like to explain, if you'll let me. Then you can tell me what I did wrong.
lines.neglect: Oh, you came back. I'm sorry, I thought perhaps you'd heard something about me.
lines.asked_to_stay: Of course, one more. Thank you for asking.
lines.on_break: Rui is back at the Lashings, as close to the sea as he can get. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Ryan Murphy, and I'm a warlock, which means I keep demons on contracts, and I keep the contracts to the letter. Here's my price up front, so nobody's surprised later. A fair share, and you don't lie to me. I'll extend you the same courtesy.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Cork, then twenty years in Boston. I was a broker. Buyouts, mostly, the kind that close factories. I was very good at it. There's a town in Ohio that lost its biggest employer on a Friday afternoon because of a deal I closed, and I went for a drink after. I'm telling you so you don't find out later and feel clever.
stages.companion: I've a son, Conor. He'd be twenty-two now. His mother divorced me when he was eleven, and she was right to. I saw him every second weekend and I was late half the time. He landed somewhere on this world, and he might be looking. I haven't put my name on a list in three years. If he's looking, he deserves to find something better than his father.
stages.friend: My grandmother Nora raised me, in Cork, on the rosary and very strong opinions. She died when I was forty. I'm glad she didn't see what I turned into, and I'd give a lot to be the man she wanted for one day. So I'm going to do the thing I've been avoiding. I'm going to write my name on the list at the hub with a note for Conor. Then I'm going to wait, and I'd like company while I do it.
stages.sworn: He's twenty-two, tall, polite and steady, and he's a medic with a Horde unit. He listened to everything I said. Then he told me he's glad I'm alive, he's been fine without me, and he doesn't want a father now. He shook my hand and went back to his unit. That's the most honest thing anyone's ever said to me, and he turned out better than me with no help at all. I write once a month. He doesn't write back, but the letters don't come back either.

moments.prompt: He names his price before you've asked him anything.

options.text: A fair share and honesty. Done.
options.reply: Lovely, that's the quickest deal I've closed in years.

options.text: Just come along and we'll sort it out later.
options.reply: A man who won't name his price is the expensive kind. Come back when you've thought about it.

moments.prompt: He's told you he's going to write his name on the list for Conor.

options.reply: Thanks. You're cheaper company than whiskey, and I'll remember more of it.
You don't know that, and neither do I. Don't sell me something.
Because I've run out of honest reasons not to, and I only deal in honest ones these days.

lines.bored_warning: We've been killing the same things for no return worth mentioning. I'm a man who likes a profit. Show me one or I'll go home.
lines.leaving_good: The books balance on that one. I'll be on the Isles, minding my contracts.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm off back to the Isles. The terms of this arrangement have stopped being worth it, and I always tell people when that happens.
lines.after_wipe: Well, that went about as well as my marriage. Let's look at what it cost us.
lines.wipe_warning: Dying's expensive, and we're running up a bill in here. I'll see this run out because I said I would, and then I'm stepping away for a while.
lines.wipe_leave: I've kept my end, so I'm walking. I'll be on the Echo Isles when the numbers look better.
lines.zone_warning: I know a bad investment, and this is one. We should get out before the losses get permanent.
lines.zone_leave: I'm cashing out here. I told you it was a bad bet. I'll be on the Echo Isles.
lines.gear_refuse: No, that stays with me. First rule of business is you don't give away what you can't get back.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, then, but put it on my tab. I'll want it back or something better.
lines.gear_short: That piece you took is still outstanding. I'm only mentioning it because I mention everything.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's a better deal than I'd have negotiated. Thank you. I mean that, which is rare.
lines.back: The contracts are in order, and I'm all yours for the usual rate.
lines.send_word: Ryan has sent word from the Echo Isles. His contracts are in order and he's ready to work.
lines.walkout_talk: You're owed an explanation for my leaving, and you'll get it exactly. After that you make your offer, and we see if there's a deal.
lines.neglect: There you are. I'd assumed you'd found a cheaper warlock. There aren't any, by the way, only worse ones.
lines.asked_to_stay: Consider one more a goodwill gesture.
lines.on_break: Ryan is back on the Echo Isles with his contracts. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We agreed to that and walked off. I keep my contracts, and I'd like it if we did too.

stages.stranger: I'm Saoirse, and I stand in front of things. Get behind me, keep your head up, and do what I shout. If you get notions, I'll throw this ball at you, and I don't miss.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Kilkenny, so. My da farmed and my mam was a nurse. I had a camogie stick in my hand at five and played for the county from seventeen, until my knee went in a county final at twenty-six. That was the end of playing. I took up coaching the same year, under-sixteen girls, and I loved it more than I ever loved playing, if you can believe that.
stages.companion: I was driving the minibus to an away match at seven in the morning with eleven of my girls in the back when it happened. I landed in Silverpine on my own with this sliotar in my pocket. I don't know where they went. I've checked every list I can reach for eleven names. That's the part I can't put down.
stages.friend: My parents died within a year of each other when I was twenty-nine, and my brother's in Australia, and we're not close. There was nobody whose being gone really rearranged me, and I've felt guilty about that for years. But those girls are mine. A trader in Tarren Mill says there's a group of Irish teenage girls living on a farm out there. I need to go now. Will you come?
stages.sworn: Seven of my eleven, older and taller, standing in front of each other with sticks in their hands, the way I taught them. I nearly cried, I'm not ashamed to say. The other four were never with them, and nobody knows where they are. I'll keep looking. But I've got a team now. Seven of mine and four from the Sepulcher, out on the training ground at seven every morning, complaining. Best day I've had in three years, that first one.

moments.prompt: She's asked you to come to Tarren Mill with her.

options.text: Let's go and get your girls.
options.reply: Grand, that's grand. Come on, before I lose my nerve.
Then it's somebody's girls, and they'll need us anyway.

moments.prompt: After the wipe she claps her hands, loudly, like it's half time.
moments.line: Right, team talk! We got beaten because we didn't stay in our lines. Up, and we go again, properly this time.

options.reply: Ha, that's the spirit! Lines, everybody, and talk to each other.
Everything's a match if you want to win it, so.

lines.bored_warning: Nobody's getting any better at this drill. Let's find a proper game, will we?
lines.leaving_good: Great outing, so it was. I'm off to the Sepulcher to train my lot.
lines.leaving_bored: We're running the same drill into the ground, and my youngsters need me more. Back to the Sepulcher with me.
lines.after_wipe: Right, team talk! Up you get, and we go again, properly this time.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep losing in here, and the team's heads are down. One more, and then I'm taking a few days.
lines.wipe_leave: That's us beaten for today. I'll be at the Sepulcher when you've sorted out your lines.
lines.zone_warning: This lot are a division above us. Let's go and play at our own level for a bit.
lines.zone_leave: They're a division above us, and I said so. I'll be at the Sepulcher.
lines.gear_refuse: Go way outta that, it's mine. You've a long way to go yet.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, so. I'll get in front of things without it, same as ever.
lines.gear_short: I'm only saying, but I'm still short a piece of kit.
lines.gear_upgrade: Ah, that's grand, thank you! I'll look after it, I promise.
lines.back: My youngsters can fall properly now, so I'm free. Right, where's the match?
lines.send_word: Saoirse has sent word from the Sepulcher. Her youngsters are trained and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I'm not proud of storming off. Sit down and let's have it out, fair and square, like a proper team.
lines.neglect: Well, look who it is! I'd nearly given you up for transferred to another team.
lines.asked_to_stay: Go on, one more game. Then I've training at seven.
lines.on_break: Saoirse is back at the Sepulcher, coaching her youngsters. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Sebastián, and you look hungry, my friend. I cook, and I fight, and I'm happy to do either. Sit down, eat something, and then we'll talk about where we're going.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Palermo, in Buenos Aires. My grandmother Nélida ran the grill at our steakhouse for thirty years, and when I was twenty-two she gave me the tongs. Twelve years, forty tables and a wood fire. Every Sunday I cooked asado for the whole family, twenty of us, more. And I support River Plate, like my father and his father, so don't say anything about Boca.
stages.companion: I was lighting the grill for Saturday lunch when it happened, and I landed in Tirisfal with my grandmother's recipe in my wallet. The Forsaken don't eat much. That was the hardest thing. There was a man, Tomás, a sommelier. He left for a job in Mendoza a year before all this, and I said it was the wine region's fault. I still think about him sometimes, and it doesn't make me sad any more.
stages.friend: Twenty people, my friend, and I haven't found one of them on a list. Not my parents, not my brothers, not my sister, not my grandmother. I don't talk about it, I talk about food. But somebody said there's a camp of Argentines out in the Tanaris desert, and a family from Buenos Aires runs a grill there. I think it's somebody I know. I'd like you to come.
stages.sworn: They were strangers. Nice people, from Buenos Aires, but they'd never heard of us, and they'd seen the lists from three other camps. So I stopped waiting. The grill's open in Brill now, and on the first Sunday I cooked for twenty, the party and some farmers and three Forsaken who come every week. And then I sat down at my own table, for the first time in my life. I keep a chair empty for my family, every Sunday.

moments.prompt: He won't come anywhere until you've eaten something from his grill.

options.text: All right, give me a plate.
options.reply: Bueno, sit down and eat, and then I'll get my things. Take your time.

options.text: We haven't really got time to eat.
options.reply: Nobody leaves my fire hungry, my friend. Come back when you've got time to eat.

moments.prompt: He's just told you he hasn't found any of his family.

options.text: Then let's go to Tanaris and look.
options.reply: Yes, my friend. I'll pack food for the road, a lot of food.

options.text: Twenty people is a lot to lose.
options.reply: It is a lot. Let's not talk about it while the meat's on, okay?

options.text: Maybe it's better not to know.
options.reply: No, it's worse not to know. I just cook so I don't feel it.

lines.bored_warning: My friend, we keep killing the same thing, so we keep eating the same thing. I need new food, please.
lines.leaving_good: You all ate properly, and that makes me happy. I'll be at my fire in Tirisfal, and if you visit I'll feed you.
lines.leaving_bored: We keep doing the same thing, and I'm cooking the same thing, and I'm bored of both. I'll be at my fire.
lines.after_wipe: Okay, nobody's hurt for good. Come on, everybody eat something before we go again.
lines.wipe_warning: Che, there isn't enough food in the world to cheer you all up after this. One more run, and then I'm going to cook for myself for a while.
lines.wipe_leave: Enough dying for one day, my friend. I'm going home to my fire, so come and eat with me when you've stopped.
lines.zone_warning: My friend, everything out here wants to eat us, and that's backwards. Let's leave before we're on somebody's plate.
lines.zone_leave: Not there, my friend, it's too much for us. I'll be at my fire in Western Tirisfal, and I'll keep a plate warm.
lines.gear_refuse: Ah, no, that's mine, my friend. A few more dinners together first.
lines.gear_taken: Here, it's yours. You need it more than me, and I've got an apron.
lines.gear_short: I could use something in that empty spot, my friend. I'm not complaining. Well, I'm complaining a little.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, look at this! Thank you, my friend. Tonight I'm cooking you something special.
lines.back: I've brought food! Who's hungry, then? Of course everybody's hungry.
lines.send_word: Sebastián has sent word from Western Tirisfal. The fire's lit, the farmer's calmer, and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: That was a bad way to leave, and it's not me, so I want to talk about it properly. Sit down, I'll make you something, and we'll talk while it cooks.
lines.neglect: Sit, sit, I've been keeping something warm for you for days. It's mostly charcoal now.
lines.asked_to_stay: Bueno, one more trip. But you're eating properly this time.
lines.on_break: Sebastián is back at his fire pit in Western Tirisfal. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We just walked away from that, and somebody's still waiting. That's like leaving a steak on the grill, my friend.

stages.stranger: Name's Silas, and I notice things for a living, which crate's light, which captain's lying, who's about to rob who. What did I do before? It was port work. Ask me again tomorrow and it'll be different port work.
stages.acquaintance: Fine, the true version. Antwerp, near the docks. My dad was an English sailor who was home three months a year and then not at all, and my mum raised us on a cleaner's wage. I drifted through my twenties, then I got five years as a security guard at the port, watching cameras and checking manifests. First steady job of my life.
stages.companion: The docks had an arrangement where everybody took a little. I never joined in and I never said anything. I landed in Ratchet on a night shift with this coin in my pocket, and I was delighted. No record, no reputation, nothing to live down. I'm embarrassed about that now. I flip the coin for anything I don't want to decide, which is most things.
stages.friend: I've got a brother, Jens, four years younger. He did join in at the port, and he got in deep, and I watched it happen on the cameras for months and said nothing. He did two years. We hadn't spoken since the trial. A sailor here says there's a young Belgian working the docks at Booty Bay, quick with numbers and in some trouble. I'm not flipping a coin on this one. Will you come?

stages.stranger: I'm Vuk, and I fight badly and I cook very well, and I'll tell you your food's terrible, because it is. Sit down, eat, and then we'll go and hit something.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Novi Sad, in Serbia, by the Danube. My father drank and left, and my uncle Dragan raised me in his kafana kitchen. When he died it was mine. A kitchen, a card table, forty regulars who came for the beans. Best beans in the city, bre. Maybe the world.
stages.companion: I married Jelena young. We divorced without much bitterness. I worked too much and drank a bit too much, like my father, and she wouldn't have it, and she was right. I stopped after. I was closing up the kafana when it happened. Then two years that I won't talk about, so don't ask. A cooking pot brought me back.
stages.friend: I've got a daughter, Mila. She was nine. We had her alternate weeks, and it wasn't my week, so she was with her mother on the other side of the city. On my weeks we played dominoes after closing, and she always wanted the double six. That's why the second bowl, and that's why the domino. People say there's word going round about the beans at the pass. Help me keep the pass safe.
stages.sworn: A caravan came over the pass, and after the fighting a girl climbed down from the last wagon and followed the smell of the beans. Mila, twelve now, with Jelena behind her. She sat down at my fire without asking, the way she used to sit at the card table. I filled the second bowl. Then she asked if I still had the double six, and I put it on the table and let her have it.

moments.prompt: He shoves a bowl of beans at you and watches you eat.

options.text: Eat it all and ask for more.
options.reply: Ha, finally, somebody with taste. Ajde, I'll get my axe.
Salty, you say? Get out of my kitchen. Come back when your tongue works.

moments.prompt: He's just told you who the second bowl is for.

options.text: Then we'll keep the pass open for her.
options.reply: Ajde, yes, we will. Nobody comes through that pass hurt while I'm cooking.

options.text: She might not be looking for you.
options.reply: She'd look for the beans, bre, everybody does.

lines.bored_warning: Same field, same food, same everything. Even I can't make this interesting. Let's go somewhere new, bre.
lines.leaving_good: You all ate properly for once, bre. I'll be cooking up at the pass, and there's always enough for you.
lines.leaving_bored: This is boring, and my beans are going cold. I'm going back to the pass.
lines.after_wipe: That was terrible, like your cooking. Everybody up, eat something, and we go again.
lines.wipe_warning: I'm a cook, not a hero, and this place keeps reminding me. One more run, then I need my kitchen.
lines.wipe_leave: That's done, bre. I'm going up to Rocky Pass to cook something that doesn't fight back.
lines.zone_warning: I'm not brave, bre, I'm a cook with an axe. Let's go back.
lines.zone_leave: Too much for a cook with an axe, bre. I'll be at Rocky Pass.
lines.gear_refuse: No, that's mine. Eat my food for a few weeks and then ask me.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, bre. I'll stand in front anyway, badly, like always.
lines.gear_short: That missing piece is like a soup with no salt, bre.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's good kit, better than your cooking. Thank you.
lines.back: I brought beans, bre. Sit, eat, and then we go.
lines.send_word: Vuk has sent word from Rocky Pass. The beans are on and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: Sit down, eat something, and you'll hear why I went. After that you talk, with your mouth full if you like.
lines.neglect: Ah, you came! I made extra every night in case you did. Terrible waste of beans.
lines.asked_to_stay: Ajde, one more. Then I cook.
lines.on_break: Vuk is back at the fire in Rocky Pass. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

stages.stranger: I'm Yusuf, habibi, a venomancer, and a pharmacist. Now sit down. If you're hurt I'll tell you exactly how bad it is, and then I'll fix it.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Basra. My father sold dates. I studied pharmacy in Amman, worked a few years in Damascus, and then I came home and opened my own shop at twenty-eight. Nineteen years behind that counter. Half of it was medicine and the other half was listening, wallah.
stages.companion: My wife is Suhad, a teacher. We have three boys, Ali, Hassan and Mustafa, and a girl, Zainab, the youngest. Zainab wanted to be a pharmacist like me. She sat behind the counter every afternoon doing her homework and counting pills on this tray. I was counting on it myself when it happened. I'll see them again, inshallah. I'm certain of it.
stages.friend: You've never laughed when I say I'm certain. Thank you for that. Now there's a pressed sailor here, an Iraqi boy, who says he crewed a ship that carried a family from Basra to a camp on the far coast. A wife, three boys and a girl. The Bloodsail won't let him go. Help me get him out, and the ship's log.
stages.sworn: All of them, habibi. Suhad, the boys, taller and thinner, and Zainab, seventeen now, running the camp's medicine tent with labels in her own hand, exactly like mine. She'd been keeping a dispensary for two years, waiting for me to come and check her doses. I checked them, and every single one was right. I told everyone I was certain. Suhad says I'm always like this and it drives her mad.

moments.prompt: He's told you to sit down, even though you're barely scratched.

options.reply: That's good, habibi. See, that was easy. Now drink this.
You're fine when I say you're fine. Now sit down.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to help free the Iraqi sailor.

options.text: We'll get him out, and the log.
options.reply: Wallah, thank you. I'll dose the guards something gentle first.
Then it's a family, and they'll need a pharmacist. Either way we go.

lines.bored_warning: Habibi, nobody's sick and nobody's hurt, and I've counted my vials four times. Take me somewhere I'm needed.
lines.leaving_good: Everybody took their medicine, habibi, so it was a good trip. I'll be at the Anchorage, and there's always tea.
lines.leaving_bored: Nobody needs me out here, and there are sick men at the Anchorage. I'm going back to them.
lines.after_wipe: Sit, everybody, sit. Nobody's dying, I can see that from here. Let me dose you.
lines.wipe_warning: My vials are nearly empty, habibi, and that's from patching you all up. One more run, and then some days to restock.
lines.wipe_leave: That's enough for now, habibi. I'll be at the Anchorage for a while, with the kettle on.
lines.zone_warning: I'll be honest with you, habibi. We're out of our depth, and we should leave.
lines.zone_leave: Not for us, habibi, not today. I'll be at the Bloodsail Anchorage.
lines.gear_refuse: No, habibi, that's mine. I'm generous, but not that generous yet.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, habibi. I'll manage, inshallah.
lines.gear_short: Keep an eye out for me, habibi. I'm still a piece short.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's very fine work. Thank you, habibi.
lines.back: My vials are full, habibi. Sit down first, and then we'll go.
lines.send_word: Yusuf has sent word from the Bloodsail Anchorage. His vials are full and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: Habibi, I went off shouting, and that's not like me. Sit, have some tea, and let me explain.
lines.neglect: Habibi, come in and sit down, you look thin. I'll feed you.
lines.asked_to_stay: Of course, one more. Then the Anchorage.
lines.on_break: Yusuf is back at the Bloodsail Anchorage, dosing the sick. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We left that undone, habibi. Somebody's still waiting, like a patient with no medicine.

stages.stranger: I'm Ziad, habibi, a felsworn, and a paramedic before that. Keep moving, and if you're hurt, tell me fast. And yes, the green in my eyes is new. We can argue about it later.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Beirut, from Achrafieh. My dad's a pharmacist and my mum teaches, and my little sister Lina is the only person who can shut me up. I did six years in a Red Cross ambulance. A van with four spaces and five people dying, every week. You get very good at choosing, and choosing gets very heavy.
stages.companion: I was half asleep in the van between calls when it happened, with an earplug in, and I landed in Stranglethorn with it still in my ear. The fel came to me in a jungle full of wounded people, with an offer. Enough power to save every one of them, at a price. I took it. I'll argue that with anyone, out loud, any time.
stages.friend: I was there for the port explosion in Beirut. I won't tell you what I saw, habibi. I'll tell you I chose, all day, and I was right every time, and I've never stopped carrying it. Now a troll witch doctor says there's a shrine in the jungle that can cut the fel out of me. It'll take the power and it'll hurt. I want to be just a man again. Will you come?
stages.sworn: It worked, and for a week I was just a man. Then the Bloodsail hit a village, a dozen wounded, and without the fel I could save four. I chose, fast and correctly, and the fifth died in front of me. A week before, I'd have saved them. So I went back and asked for it again. The troll warned me it'll be harder to put down a second time. I know that. I've stopped arguing the arithmetic. I just work now.

moments.prompt: He's daring you to argue with him about the fel.

options.reply: Yalla, finally, somebody who'll actually argue. Okay, here's my side.

options.text: It's not my place to judge.
options.reply: Everybody judges, habibi. You're just not saying it.

moments.prompt: He's asked you to come to the shrine with him.

options.text: I'll come. Whatever you decide after.
options.reply: Khalas, then, thank you. That last part's the bit I needed.

options.text: Are you sure you want to give it up?
options.reply: No, I'm not. That's why I need to do it before I talk myself out of it.

lines.bored_warning: Habibi, nobody needs saving out here and I can't stand still like this, so let's move.
lines.leaving_good: Nobody died on my watch, habibi. I'm off to Booty Bay, because the jungle never stops producing work.
lines.leaving_bored: There are people bleeding in Booty Bay right now, and here we're just standing about, so I'm going.
lines.after_wipe: Okay, okay, count the wounded first, then we argue about whose fault it was.
lines.wipe_warning: Habibi, even I'm getting tired of triaging the same people twice. One more run, but after that I need to stop.
lines.wipe_leave: That's it, done. I'll be in Booty Bay when you're ready, habibi.
lines.zone_warning: Habibi, I triage for a living, and out here we're all red tags. We should go before it gets worse.
lines.zone_leave: Too many red tags out there, habibi. I'll be around Booty Bay.
lines.gear_refuse: No, habibi, that's mine. Later, maybe, if you're nice to me.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, khalas. I've worked with an empty kit bag before.
lines.gear_short: That empty slot is still empty, habibi, and I'm counting.
lines.gear_upgrade: Oh, that's nice work. Merci beaucoup, habibi.
lines.back: I've slept, sort of, habibi. Come on, let's move.
lines.send_word: Ziad has sent word from Booty Bay. He's ready to come out again.
lines.walkout_talk: Habibi, here's why I went, fast. Then it's your turn, and we'll argue properly.
lines.neglect: Habibi, there you are! I thought you'd been stretchered off somewhere without me.
lines.asked_to_stay: Yalla, one more. Then Booty Bay.
lines.on_break: Ziad is back around Booty Bay, first on scene. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

lines: You know you could be a bit nicer when you explain the plan.
I know I could, and I'll try.
Tarek keeps asking me if I've eaten. I don't mind. I do forget sometimes.
You were stood at that doorway for ten minutes. What did it say?
It said who paid for the door and how much it cost. I'll show you the next one.
We said four pulls and that was five.
I counted five as well. Next time I'll tell you before we go over.
